issue.title: Add Stratum wide default values for copts, linkopts and testing copts

repository.name: stratum
repository.description: Stratum is an open source silicon-independent switch operating system for software defined networks.

issue.body:
The specific flag values are taken verbatim from [Abseil](https://github.com/abseil/abseil-cpp/blob/518f17501e6156f7921fbb9b68a1e420bcb10bc5/absl/copts/GENERATED_copts.bzl).

This will allow us to transition from global copts in `.bazelrc` to per-target specific options. 
Compiler matching is performed based on the `"@bazel_tools//tools/cpp:compiler"` flag value. This values is always defined, even when the `--compiler=foo` CLI flag is not set.

The default set of options is applied to all `stratum_cc_library` and `stratum_cc_binary` targets. Currently it can not be overwritten, just extended. Since not all targets use the `stratum_*` rules yet, we can use that as a toggle to disable extended checking for impacted targets, until fixed later.

Fixes #102

issue.title: bazel: Assume default compiler is gcc
issue.body:
Commit Message:

It is impossible to turn on the "//bazel/gcc_build" config setting on Bazel 3.7.x, see:

   https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/12707

GCC 9, which is the default in Ubuntu 20.04, requires the -Wno-maybe-uninitialized for
@com_googlesource_quiche//:quic_core_framer_lib to compile successfully.

Mitigate by assuming the default "compiler" is GCC. Clang is properly recognized by Bazel, so it is not affected by this.

Signed-off-by: Jarno Rajahalme <jarno@covalent.io>

Additional Description: See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/12707

Risk Level: Medium, non-GCC compilers may not implement -Wno-maybe-uninitialized, and may start to fail if not recognized by Bazel.

Testing: Tested compilations with both GCC and clang, and observed that -Wno-maybe-uninitialized is present with GCC but not with clang.

Docs Changes:

Release Notes: Fix compilation with GCC by assuming it is the default compiler.

issue.title: Targets with `target_compatible_with = ["@bazel_tools//tools/cpp:clang"]` are always skipped

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
### Description of the problem / feature request:

Targets with `target_compatible_with = ["@bazel_tools//tools/cpp:clang"]` are skipped even if `CC` is `clang`.

### Bugs: what's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.

```shell
$ touch WORKSPACE
$ touch empty.cc
$ cat << EOF > BUILD
cc_test(
    name = "empty",
    srcs = ["empty.cc"],
    target_compatible_with = [
        "@bazel_tools//tools/cpp:clang",
    ],
)
EOF
$ bazel test //...
...
//:empty                                                                SKIPPED
...
$ CC=clang bazel test //...
...
//:empty                                                                SKIPPED
...
```
### What operating system are you running Bazel on?

Linux
### What's the output of `bazel info release`?

Tested with:
```
release 4.0.0
release 5.0.0-pre.20210728.1
```

###  Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

- #12707, but this concerns the compiler_flag target `@bazel_tools//tools/cpp:compiler`, which ~cannot~ can be used with `target_compatible_with` (see comment below). 

The auto-detected host platform definition written in `LocalConfigPlatformFunction.java` does not include a constraint for a compiler.

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

body:
@oquenchil I have a (simple) fix for this bug, but am wondering about your thoughts on backwards compatibility here: If `compiler` starts to have the value `"gcc"` instead of `"compiler"` for `gcc`, this could mess with existing uses of `select`. 

Envoy [may break](https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/pull/14857#issuecomment-769452791), but would certainly welcome the fix based on the discussion on that PR. Abseil would not break as they treat `gcc` as the default case.

issue.title: How to tell absl's bazel script which compiler (gcc/clang)
issue.body:
Hi,

I've got an interesting problem, where I've specified my own (gcc based) toolchain, and this is preventing me from using absl's bazel integration. In particular, absl is detecting that I'm using gcc, and starts passing clang-only flags, and... kBOOM!

How does absl figure which compiler I'm using, and how do I tell it to assume gcc?

Thanks

body: @fmeum , can you describe what your simple fix is? Is there a way to simply tell bazel which compiler to use?

No. I think it's fine. This would be a bug fix. Ideally the change would be checked in together with a script that runs buildozer (or some regex) over a project and fixes the places that need fixing. But if that's not possible then properly describing how it can break and what the instructions for fixing it are should be enough.

issue.title: Mark gcc as `gcc` instead of `compiler` in Unix CC toolchain

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
This makes it possible to detect gcc specifically via a `config_setting` for the `@bazel_tools//tools/cpp:compiler` flag with value `gcc`.

RELNOTES: The `@bazel_tools//tools/cpp:compiler` flag now has the value `gcc` if the configured compiler is detected to be gcc rather than the generic value `compiler`. A branch for `gcc` may have to be added to `select` statements that do not have a default case that handles gcc appropriately.

Fixes #12707
